newsitem.title: CANADA: Inco union sees lengthy Sudbury strike.
newsitem.headline: Inco union sees lengthy Sudbury strike.

text.p: The union representing Inco Ltd's striking workers in Sudbury, Ontario said on Wednesday it could be months before the labor dispute was resolved.

"I don't see that happening short term anyway. I think this strike is going to be a couple of months," Wayne Fraser, chief negotiator for United Steelworkers of America local 6500, said in a telephone interview.
Fraser said the company and union were far apart on issues such as wages, pensions, vacation pay and contracting out.
Inco's 4,670 unionized Sudbury workers went on strike at midnight on Monday, after voting 60.4 percent against a contract offer endorsed by union leaders last Friday.
Monetary issues aside, Fraser said some union members feared losing bargaining power when Inco's massive Voisey's Bay nickel deposit begins production in late 1999.
"Our membership were really concerned that our bargaining power will be different come the year 2000. Bargaining is good now, they're saying, so let's take them to the bank," Fraser said.
Mining analysts have said a prolonged shutdown would be bullish for nickel prices.
According to Inco's 1997 production plan, the Ontario division was expected to produce about 230 million pounds of nickel, about 200 million pounds of copper and about four million pounds of cobalt.

Inco's Port Colborne, Ontario refinery, which processes cobalt, precious metals and electro-nickel, was not affected by the Sudbury strike. Unionized workers at the refinery approved the contract on Monday.
Inco's stock was off 0.35 at 44.30 on the Toronto Stock Exchange on Wednesday.
